summary.headline: Sagility Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29.1% YoY in INR to ₹20,243 million, with FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 25.3%, ahead of guidance.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹20,243 million ($222.1 million), up 29.1% YoY in INR and 22.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 19.4% CC. Adjusted EBITDA was ₹5,036 million (24.9% margin) and adjusted PAT ₹3,069 million (15.2%). For FY26, revenue reached ₹71,929 million (up 29.1% INR, 23.6% CC; organic 15% CC) and adjusted EBITDA was 25.3%, ahead of the Q3 guidance, helped by higher-than-expected seasonal open enrolment and AEP revenue. Management guided FY27 organic growth to low double digits in CC and adjusted EBITDA margin of 24% to 25%, tracking the upper end if FX holds.

financial_highlights.change: +29.1% YoY INR; +22.2% CC; +25.8% INR organic excl. BroadPath
Includes one-time employee bonus worth ~1.7% of EBITDA margin
+29.1% YoY INR; +23.6% CC; organic +20.1% INR, +15% CC
~110 bps decline vs FY25, attributed to full-year BroadPath impact
Up from 86 days in Q3; ~4 days from reclassification, no working capital impact

financial_highlights.value: 24% to 25% guided for FY26 and FY27

segments.name: Payers
segments.commentary: Contributed 89.7% of FY26 revenue; BroadPath (predominantly payer, largely onshore delivery) lifted the payer mix.

segments.name: Providers
segments.commentary: Contributed 10.3% of FY26 revenue; management says provider business grew YoY in FY26, with RCM engagements, effort- and contingency-based pricing, and larger end-to-end deals in discussion.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to low double digits in constant currency, on an organic basis; any acquisitions would be additional.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided at 24% to 25%, likely toward the upper end if the rupee stays near current levels.
AI-driven revenue compression expected at about 2% in FY27, versus the historical 1% to 1.5%.
Debt to be fully repaid by end of FY27; a final dividend of ₹0.10 per share recommended, with no firm commitment on higher payouts.
Seasonal split of H2 to H1 expected to move to about 54.5% to 55% vs 45%, recurring each year.
Wage hike cycle moved to April-March from FY27; one-time bonus in Q4 FY26 covers the gap.
capex_capacity: Cash of ₹9,038 million to fund AI and domain capabilities and keep M&A options open.
New ESOP pool for about 3.3% of equity, subject to shareholder approval; grants annually with vesting over three years, plus two-year exercise window; FY27 P&L impact to be disclosed next quarter.
Share of US (onshore) revenue rising; BroadPath delivery is largely onshore.
demand_pricing: Q4 signed $30.7 million of potential steady-state ACV across 18 existing clients and two new clients; management said roughly $130 million cumulative ACV over FY26 quarters.
Qualitative pipeline of about ₹570 to ₹575 million TCV in submitted proposals; more managed-service, multi-year deals with longer decision cycles.
Top five clients grew 11.9% (11.7% in the earlier remark) in FY26, versus 15% company-level CC organic growth; nine clients now exceed $20 million (four in FY23).
Seasonal revenue (AEP and open enrolment) was 6% of FY26 revenue vs 3% in FY25, versus about 5.5% guided; split equally across Q3 and Q4.
Added 17 new clients in FY26, including regional plans and Blues; top three concentration below 60%.
Management said about 7% to 8% of FY27 growth is already factored in based on prior trends.
Medicare Advantage final rate increase 2.48% for CY27 (preliminary was almost flat).

qa_highlights.question: Will AI reduce future revenue, and how is the company adapting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI will lower client costs and reduce some revenue, but it expects market-share gains; organic growth is still seen in double digits, with several AI use cases implemented.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation: will dividends rise given the debt payoff and higher cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt to be repaid in FY27, funds kept for M&A (payer or provider, capability or client-access deals such as BroadPath); dividend to be reviewed with no firm commitment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base for FY27 revenue and the cumulative ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative ACV was about $130 million, but ramp timing, volume changes, AI reductions and geographic mix all affect conversion; roughly 7% to 8% growth is seen as already factored in.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin guidance of 24% to 25% below FY26's 25.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds include wage hikes funded by FX, a rising US (lower-margin) revenue mix and possible price reductions; top end of the range expected if FX holds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance low double digits when organic growth was 15%? Is AI compression higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is organic. AI compression is expected at about 2% in FY27 versus 1% to 1.5% historically, and deal timing is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 attrition higher, and will other expenses moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Attrition rose because seasonal headcount exited after open enrolment. Other expenses rose on IT and AI investment plus some asset write-offs from centre rationalisation; management expects them to stay high.

risks_watch: Deal timing unpredictability as managed-service and transformation deals take longer than traditional RFPs.
AI-led productivity compression rising to about 2% in FY27 from 1% to 1.5%.
Rupee depreciation level: needed to fund wage hikes and drives the margin upside; a smaller move would weigh on margins.
Rising onshore (US) revenue mix, which carries lower margins than offshore work.
ESOP cost (3.3% pool) to hit P&L from FY27; quantum to be disclosed next quarter.
Medicaid growth moderation after Big Beautiful Bill changes; ACA subsidy uncertainty.
Q1 seasonality and attrition pattern following the surge in Q3 and Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 execution and the pipeline, but deliberately conservative on FY27, with guidance framed as what can be met and tied to visibility and FX. Management was evasive on specifics like the exact cumulative ACV and the ESOP P&L impact, deferring them to the next call.
key_quotes: We are confident of growing in the low double-digits in constant currency for FY '27.
Our guidance for adjusted EBITDA margin is between 24% and 25%.
So the guidance of low double-digits that we are giving is for organic growth.
Our top five grew at 11.9%, whereas at a company level we grew at 15%.

growth.why: FY27 organic growth guided to low double digits in constant currency (midpoint ~11%), with 24-25% EBITDA margin; backed partly by Q4 ACV signings ($30.7M across 18 existing and 2 new clients) and a ~7-8% already-factored contribution, but no specific capacity or contracted order numbers beyond pipeline, so partial backing.
